settings.text: We start by understanding where your business is now, what is holding it back, and what needs to change before we build anything.

Before we touch design, copy, ads, or automation, we first look at the foundation. This step helps us uncover the real bottlenecks in your current customer journey, so we do not solve the wrong problem.

We review your offer, audience, positioning, website, current marketing activity, and conversion points. The goal is to create a clear picture of what is working, what is missing, and where the biggest opportunities are.
We turn the insights from discovery into a clear plan that defines what to build, why it matters, and how it will support business growth.

A strong website or marketing system should not be based on guesswork. In this phase, we define the direction, priorities, messaging, structure, and conversion strategy.

This gives every decision a clear purpose. Instead of adding random sections, features, or campaigns, we create a focused plan that connects your business goals with the needs of your ideal customer.
We design and develop the assets, pages, systems, and touchpoints needed to turn the strategy into a working customer journey.

Once the strategy is clear, we move into execution. This is where the visual direction, copy, website, landing pages, forms, booking flows, and technical setup come together.

The focus is not just on making things look good. Every part of the build should help visitors understand your value, trust your business, and take the next step.
We prepare everything for launch, test the full experience, and make sure the system is ready to receive real visitors and leads.

A launch is not just putting a website online. Before going live, we check the complete journey from first impression to final conversion.

We test the pages, forms, links, tracking, responsiveness, speed, and key user actions. This helps reduce friction and prevents simple mistakes from damaging the first impression.
After launch, we review performance, identify improvement opportunities, and refine the system based on real behavior.

The first version is only the starting point. Once people start interacting with the website or funnel, we can see what actually happens.

We look at traffic, clicks, conversions, drop-off points, and lead quality. From there, we improve the weak spots and strengthen the parts that already work. This is how the system becomes more effective over time.

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  /**
   * Find all instances of this pattern on the page.
   */
  const scrollSpySections = document.querySelectorAll(
    ".bm-how-it-works-28__container"
  );

  if (!scrollSpySections.length) return;

  /**
   * Inject a temporary measuring style.
   *
   * Why?
   * Sticky cards can report their current sticky viewport position
   * instead of their original document position.
   *
   * When we need to calculate the scroll target, we temporarily disable
   * sticky positioning, measure the true layout position, then restore sticky.
   */
  const measuringStyle = document.createElement("style");

  measuringStyle.textContent = `
    html.bm-how-it-works-28-is-measuring .bm-how-it-works-28-card {
      position: relative !important;
      top: auto !important;
    }
  `;

  document.head.appendChild(measuringStyle);

  /**
   * Store all working scroll-spy instances.
   */
  const instances = [];

  /**
   * Get the true document position of a sticky card.
   *
   * This is the key fix.
   *
   * We temporarily disable sticky positioning before measuring.
   * That gives us the card's original position in the document flow.
   */
  function getTrueDocumentTop(element) {
    document.documentElement.classList.add("bm-how-it-works-28-is-measuring");

    const top = element.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY;

    document.documentElement.classList.remove("bm-how-it-works-28-is-measuring");

    return top;
  }

  scrollSpySections.forEach((scrollSpy) => {
    /**
     * Select the actual anchor links.
     *
     * The href is on:
     * .bm-how-it-works-28-nav-item__link
     *
     * Not on:
     * .bm-how-it-works-28-nav-item
     */
    const navLinks = Array.from(
      scrollSpy.querySelectorAll(".bm-how-it-works-28-nav-item__link")
    );

    /**
     * Match every nav link to its corresponding card.
     */
    const sections = navLinks
      .map((link) => {
        const id = link.getAttribute("href");

        if (!id || !id.startsWith("#")) return null;

        const section = scrollSpy.querySelector(id);

        if (!section) return null;

        return {
          id,
          link,
          section,
        };
      })
      .filter(Boolean);

    if (!sections.length) return;

    /**
     * Add/remove active classes.
     *
     * Adds .is-active to:
     * 1. The active anchor link
     * 2. The parent nav item
     */
    function setActiveLink(activeId) {
      navLinks.forEach((link) => {
        const isActive = link.getAttribute("href") === activeId;
        const navItem = link.closest(".bm-how-it-works-28-nav-item");

        link.classList.toggle("is-active", isActive);

        if (navItem) {
          navItem.classList.toggle("is-active", isActive);
        }
      });
    }

    /**
     * Detect which card should be active while scrolling.
     */
    function updateActiveSection() {
      const triggerLine = window.innerHeight * 0.25;

      let activeSection = sections[0];

      sections.forEach((item) => {
        const rect = item.section.getBoundingClientRect();

        if (rect.top <= triggerLine) {
          activeSection = item;
        }
      });

      setActiveLink(activeSection.id);
    }

    /**
     * Smooth scroll when clicking nav links.
     *
     * Important:
     * We use window.scrollTo() with a measured document position.
     * We do not use scrollIntoView(), because sticky elements can confuse it.
     */
    navLinks.forEach((link) => {
      link.addEventListener(
        "click",
        (event) => {
          const targetId = link.getAttribute("href");

          if (!targetId || !targetId.startsWith("#")) return;

          const targetSection = scrollSpy.querySelector(targetId);

          if (!targetSection) return;

          /**
           * Stop the normal anchor jump.
           */
          event.preventDefault();

          /**
           * Stop Bricks' own anchor behavior from fighting this script.
           *
           * This matters because your links include:
           * data-brx-anchor="true"
           */
          event.stopPropagation();

          /**
           * Offset controls where the card lands.
           *
           * Increase this if you have a sticky header.
           * Decrease this if the card stops too low.
           */
          const offset = 120;

          /**
           * Measure the true original document position of the card.
           */
          const targetPosition = getTrueDocumentTop(targetSection) - offset;

          /**
           * Scroll there in one click.
           */
          window.scrollTo({
            top: targetPosition,
            behavior: "smooth",
          });

          /**
           * Optional:
           * Update the active class immediately after click.
           */
          setActiveLink(targetId);
        },
        true
      );
    });

    instances.push({
      updateActiveSection,
    });

    updateActiveSection();
  });

  /**
   * Update all scroll-spy instances on scroll.
   */
  window.addEventListener(
    "scroll",
    () => {
      instances.forEach((instance) => {
        instance.updateActiveSection();
      });
    },
    { passive: true }
  );

  /**
   * Recalculate active sections on resize.
   */
  window.addEventListener("resize", () => {
    instances.forEach((instance) => {
      instance.updateActiveSection();
    });
  });
});
</script>
